newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Indices quiet as rolls dominate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Indices quiet as rolls dominate.

text.p: Major U.S. stock index option trading was modest on Thursday heading into the expiration of May options, with much of the action dominated by investors rolling positions out of expiring May, traders said.
"I've been trading rolls back and forth," one S&P 500 index .SPX options trader said. "There hasn't been anything going on."
He added that volatility in June SPX options had eased slightly as the market waffled around unchanged levels.
In afternoon trading, the spot SPX index was up 1.87 at 837.91 and June S&P 500 futures were up 0.85 at 840.80.
One trader in S&P 100 index options said activity in that pit also was fairly quiet.
The SPX options trader said most investors were on the sidelines ahead of next Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting unit.
The heaviest volume in SPX options was in the May 840 and 850 calls and the May 835 and 830 puts.
The biggest open interest was in the in-the-money May 820 call, which had traded just 500 contracts by afternoon. Open interest was 16,281 through Wednesday.
In the OEX, the heaviest volume was in the May 820 puts, which traded more than 14,000 contracts.
The OEX May 815 and 810 puts also were busy, as were the May 820, 825, 830 and 835 calls.
May SPX options finish trading Thursday and will settle at Friday's opening. May OEX options finish trading Friday and settle Saturday morning.
